scope: Final plan-only closure audit of PLAN.md and README.md against R-01 through R-16, the complete owner/agent journey, IDEATION, BUILD, MAINTENANCE, DEEP-RESEARCH, IMPROVEMENT, exception-driven human involvement, engineering-first/GTM boundaries, dogfooding, and readability. I read requirements-traceability.md, round-2-resolution.md, all six round-2 review JSON files, all four round-1 resolution memos, and the evidence-repair register, manifest, synthesis coverage, material-claims register, cutoff note, and legacy evidence matrix. The removed prototype and absence of implementation proof were accepted by design; future proof gates were reviewed as plan contracts and were not treated as already passed.
strengths: The plan is explicit that it is plan-only, that the legacy evidence is structurally audited but not semantically or provenance validated, and that a fresh immutable run plus human semantic review blocks implementation rather than being claimed complete.

R-01 through R-16 all have identifiable plan sections, roadmap increments, validation classes, and human gates. The sole-roadmap rule and revised traceability register now agree on the PostgreSQL-before-write, second-repository, improvement, and GTM order.

The top-level walkthrough gives a clear idea-to-outcome narrative across durable conversation, typed planning, fenced execution, clean verification, review, effect reconciliation, observation, cleanup, maintenance, research, and improvement.

The plan defines strong future proof gates for PostgreSQL mutation, consumer release integrity, sandbox selection, research checkpoint reuse, governed improvement, second-repository isolation, domain extraction, and GTM no-go conditions without claiming that those gates passed.

Dogfooding is separated from candidate evaluation, consumer releases are pinned and reversible, raw feedback stays local by default, and the engineering-first boundary keeps GTM read-only/proposal-only until a separate domain decision.

findings.title: The supposedly exception-driven human policy still requires a human READY approval for every build admission
findings.requirement: R-09/P-09 requires humans to be involved only for genuine authority, ambiguity, risk, confidence, exception, or recovery needs, while safe delegated work proceeds without a per-item human gate.

files: PLAN.md:86-107 (only a qualified human principal may issue an Approval)
PLAN.md:252-258 (the engine says it asks only on enumerated need, and READY approvals are human-issued)
PLAN.md:312 (every admission validates a current READY approval)
PLAN.md:374 (BUILD always obtains exact-digest READY)
PLAN.md:395-396 (a later R1 profile may auto-merge, but the READY gate is not relaxed)
review/requirements-traceability.md:R-09/P-09

reproduction: Choose a mature R0/R1 task with clear intent, strong oracle, tested rollback, no conflict, and authority already delegated by protected policy.
Section 10 says this case should take a reversible default without asking a human.
Follow BUILD and admission: both still require a current exact-digest READY Approval, and the authority table permits only a qualified human principal to issue it.
Even enabling the later R1 auto-merge profile removes only the merge interaction, not the per-item READY interaction.
findings.impact: The planned implementation cannot deliver exception-driven operation. Every build stops for a human even when none of the plan's human-needed predicates is true. This directly leaves R-09 incomplete and undermines maintenance and low-risk dogfood autonomy.
findings.recommendation: Define a distinct, protected delegation/admission-authority record for closed R0/R1 profiles. Bind it to exact scope, factory/policy version, command/effect ceiling, risk, oracle, rollback, sample/window, expiry, revocation, stop rules, and audit. Permit the controller to produce READY only from canonical state under that delegation when every human-needed predicate is false. Keep per-item human Approval mandatory for R2-R4, ambiguity, exceptions, unknown effects, authority expansion, and any changed bound input.
findings.verification: Add decision-table and journey fixtures showing one eligible delegated R0/R1 item reaches admission without a human request, while each enumerated human-needed condition deterministically creates a bounded wait. Prove delegation expiry, changed inputs, risk escalation, failed oracle/rollback, or revoked policy restores the human gate.

findings.title: The canonical projection does not define how concurrent IMPROVEMENT machines combine into one work state
findings.requirement: R-08/P-08 and R-12/P-12 require a total, executable lifecycle projection for the orthogonal candidate, rollout, attempt, and control-health machines, with no implementation-defined shortcut or unsafe precedence.

files: PLAN.md:228-236 (four orthogonal improvement machines can hold states concurrently)
PLAN.md:352-366 (the mapping claims to be state-based and total but maps each component state independently to one canonical state)
PLAN.md:364 (`DISABLED->BLOCKED`, `OFFLINE_RUNNING->VERIFYING`, and `HEALTHY->OBSERVING` can all apply at the same time)
review/round-2/security-improvement.json:SECIMP-R2-001
review/round-2/requirements-journey.json:R2-RJ-001
review/round-2-resolution.md:items 7, 11, and 20

reproduction: Take an improvement candidate in OFFLINE_RUNNING while rollout remains DISABLED and control health remains HEALTHY, a normal combination before enablement.
The published row projects those simultaneous states to VERIFYING, BLOCKED, and OBSERVING respectively.
No tuple-to-state composition function, precedence rule, allowed tuple invariant, or atomic multi-machine transition specifies which canonical state is authoritative.
A later health transition can likewise imply OBSERVING->BLOCKED even when the candidate projection is VERIFYING.
findings.impact: The compiler cannot generate one deterministic work projection or prove legal canonical edges. Implementers must invent precedence, which can hide a control-health block, misstate readiness, or create an illegal shortcut around improvement gates. The prior total-mapping and orthogonal-lifecycle findings are therefore not fully closed.
findings.recommendation: Define the IMPROVEMENT projection as an explicit function over a versioned tuple such as `(candidate_state, rollout_state, attempt_state, control_health_state, cleanup_state)`. Enumerate allowed tuples or deterministic precedence, and require each component transition to yield a legal canonical edge or stutter. Control-health failure and unresolved rollback/cleanup must dominate success/readiness. Reject unreachable or multiply projected tuples at compile time.
findings.verification: Generate the reachable product state space for all four machines. Assert that every reachable tuple has exactly one canonical projection, every component edge maps to one legal canonical edge/stutter, and telemetry degradation, stale evidence, abort, rollback failure, and cleanup cannot project as READY, MERGED, or DONE.

findings.title: Repository identity remains mandatory in two normative contracts despite the typed cross-domain ScopeRef correction
findings.requirement: R-15/P-15 and the addressed CDD-R2-004 finding require a domain-neutral kernel in which repository identity is mandatory only for engineering repository authority and cannot be fabricated as the owner of account-, consent-, campaign-, subject-, or environment-scoped data.

files: PLAN.md:121-123 (§5.1 correctly makes tenant plus typed ScopeRef normative and repository conditional)
PLAN.md:140 (§6 still says each artifact must contain repository_id)
PLAN.md:402 (§16 still says every stored, queued, cached, object-stored, and audited record carries repository_id)
PLAN.md:434-440 (§18 says the neutral kernel has no repository-only assumption and repository ID cannot authorize GTM data)
review/round-2/cross-domain-dogfood.json:CDD-R2-004
review/round-2-resolution.md:item 19

reproduction: Model the read-only GTM research artifact explicitly allowed by §18 with tenant and a consent/account ScopeRef but no repository authority.
It satisfies §§5.1 and 18, but violates the closed artifact envelope in §6 and the universal tenant-boundary invariant in §16 because both require repository_id.
Adding an arbitrary repository_id would in turn violate the rule that repository identity cannot substitute for domain authority.
findings.impact: A conforming compiler/schema cannot represent the planned repository-independent domain artifacts without either rejecting them or inventing misleading authority. This directly leaves the future cross-domain requirement and the claimed CDD-R2-004 closure inconsistent.
findings.recommendation: Replace the universal `repository_id` fields in §§6 and 16 with mandatory `tenant_id` plus typed `ScopeRef`; require repository/installation IDs only for the engineering repository scope variant. Define composite keys, idempotency namespaces, object prefixes, audit fields, and authorization from the complete typed scope, not always from repository identity.
findings.verification: Schema fixtures must accept an engineering artifact with repository scope and a repository-independent GTM research artifact with its required domain scope; reject a missing domain authority and reject repository ID as authorization for account/contact/campaign data. A normative-text check must find no remaining universal repository requirement outside the engineering scope variant.

findings.title: The normative owner interface still has no command for several required factory decisions
findings.requirement: R-03, R-10, R-12, and the addressed R2-RJ-004 finding require a complete Issue/CLI owner journey in which each required decision has an authenticated action, displayed exact subject, durable event, recovery response, and next step.

files: PLAN.md:262-282 (§10.1 command table)
PLAN.md:360 and 368-370 (IDEATION requires DECISION_REVIEW -> ACCEPTED -> HANDOFF)
PLAN.md:363 and 380-386 (DEEP-RESEARCH requires DECISION_REVIEW)
PLAN.md:364 and 388-390 (IMPROVEMENT requires curation, enablement, canary, and promotion decisions)
review/round-2/requirements-journey.json:R2-RJ-004
review/round-2-resolution.md:item 14

reproduction: Read the normative command table: it has start ideation/research, answer, status, approve READY, code-head review, exception, merge, and operational commands.

There is no command/event that accepts or rejects a DecisionRecord and triggers IDEATION handoff, accepts or requests changes to a research synthesis bound to its evidence digests, or records improvement curation/enablement/canary/promotion decisions bound to their manifests.
The generic READY approval is a BUILD admission decision, and the exact-head review command is a code review; neither specifies those other decision subjects or resulting factory transitions.
findings.impact: The backend states are defined, but the full owner/agent journey still has interaction gaps. Implementers must invent channel semantics and receipts at the most important handoffs, so the claimed R2-RJ-004 closure is incomplete even though the plan remains fail-closed in prose.
findings.recommendation: Extend §10.1 with typed accept/request-changes/deny commands for DecisionRecord, ResearchDecision, curation, ImprovementEnablementDecision, canary admission/widening, and promotion. For each, name the displayed digest/diff, eligible principal/quorum, durable event, stale/error behavior, resulting transition, and resume/recovery path. Reuse one generic decision command only if its closed subject types and transition table are explicit.
findings.verification: Paper-test one full ideation handoff, research handoff, failed curation, approved canary, denied widening, and approved promotion. Every action must map to one authenticated command and one durable exact-subject receipt; stale subjects and silence must not advance state.

findings.title: The reader-visible walkthrough has broken and duplicate step numbering
findings.requirement: The primary plan should remain readable as the sole end-to-end implementation contract.

files: PLAN.md:18-29 (§2 numbers the sequence 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 9, 10, 11)

findings.reproduction: Read §2 in order and observe the missing step 2 and duplicate step 9.
findings.impact: This does not change authority or safety semantics, but it makes the main onboarding walkthrough harder to cite and weakens plan readability.
findings.recommendation: Renumber the walkthrough sequentially and keep stable anchors if other documents cite individual steps.
findings.verification: The rendered walkthrough has one strictly increasing sequence with no duplicate or missing number.

residual_uncertainty: No implementation exists by design. This audit does not claim that any future compiler, storage gate, sandbox, factory, or pilot test passes.

The evidence corpus remains structurally audited but has unverified legacy retrieval provenance and no completed semantic review. PLAN §4 and Increment 0 correctly make the fresh immutable run and human semantic review future blocking gates.

Local thresholds, owner burden, product usefulness, recovery behavior, safe automation rate, and GTM value remain pilot questions. Their absence as passed evidence is not a plan-only defect where the plan requires predeclared decisions.
Aside from the findings above, R-01 through R-16 have a plan-level contract and future validation location; implementation completion remains intentionally 0/16.
